evals.prompt: I have a Node.js Express app in this repo (package.json with an Express dependency, app entrypoint at src/server.js, listens on port 3000). There are no Docker files yet. Please containerize it so I can build and ship it.
evals.expected_output: A modern multi-stage Dockerfile with the syntax frontend line first, version ARGs at top, hardened base images, a .dockerignore derived from .gitignore plus Docker additions, a docker-bake.hcl, and the assistant asking whether to also add a compose.yaml since this is first-time Docker setup.
expectations: The Dockerfile's first line is the frontend directive `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` (pinned to :1, not :1.0).
Base image versions are declared as global ARGs before the first FROM, and all FROM stages use explicit AS names.
The Dockerfile uses a hardened/minimal base (Chainguard cgr.dev or Docker Hardened Images dhi.io) at least for the final runtime stage, via a multi-stage build.
A .dockerignore is created that excludes .git and common secrets/junk, and reflects starting from the project's .gitignore.
A docker-bake.hcl file is created with at least one target referencing the Dockerfile and a tag.
Every external FROM image is pinned to both a tag and a digest (@sha256:...), or a clearly-marked digest placeholder with instructions to resolve it (e.g. via regctl), rather than a bare mutable tag.
Because no Docker files existed before, the assistant asks the user whether they also want a compose.yaml rather than silently creating or skipping one.

evals.prompt: Write me a Dockerfile for a Go microservice. The module builds with `go build ./cmd/api` and the binary serves HTTP on 8080. I want the smallest, most secure production image you can reasonably make.
evals.expected_output: A multi-stage Dockerfile using a Chainguard go -dev (or DHI) build stage and a distroless static final stage, with the syntax line first, version ARGs, BuildKit cache mounts for the Go build, CGO disabled, and an exec-form ENTRYPOINT.
expectations: The Dockerfile's first line is `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1`.
It is a multi-stage build whose final stage is a distroless/static hardened image (e.g. cgr.dev/chainguard/static) with no shell or package manager.
The Go version (and any base versions) are declared as ARGs and FROM stages are named with AS.
The build uses at least one BuildKit feature appropriate to Go builds (RUN --mount=type=cache for the Go build/module cache, or a bind mount), rather than a plain RUN go build with no cache.

Every external FROM image (build and runtime stages) is pinned to both a tag and a digest (@sha256:...), or a clearly-marked digest placeholder with resolve instructions, rather than a bare mutable tag.
The final stage uses exec-form ENTRYPOINT or CMD (JSON array) because the distroless image has no shell.

evals.prompt: Modernize my Docker setup. My Dockerfile starts with `FROM node:18` and has no syntax line. My docker-compose.yml has `version: "3.8"` at the top and uses a bind mount `- ./src:/app/src` for live code reloading during development. Please bring these up to current best practices.
evals.expected_output: An updated Dockerfile with the frontend directive added and modern structure, plus the compose file renamed to compose.yaml with the obsolete version key removed and the dev bind mount replaced by a develop.watch sync configuration.
expectations: The updated Dockerfile gains `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` as its first line.
The obsolete top-level `version:` key is removed from the compose file.
The compose file is named (or renamed to) compose.yaml rather than docker-compose.yml.

The source bind mount used for live reload is replaced with a develop.watch configuration using action: sync (file sync over bind mount), and the assistant notes `docker compose watch` as the run command.
The assistant explains the key changes and why each modernization matters.
